********** Addended Report ***********

CLINICAL DATA: 
Left sided brain lesion in a 61 year old female with a history of invasive 
ductal carcinoma of breast. 
 
 
FINAL DIAGNOSIS: 
BRAIN, LEFT PARIETAL (SPECIMENS A AND B): 
METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA. SEE NOTE. 
 
NOTE: The tumor is strongly positive for Cytokeratin 7 and Her-2neu (complete 
membranous staining), focally positive for GCDFP-15, faintly positive for 
progesterone receptor and negative for estrogen receptor,  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  and Cytokeratin 
20. The morphology and immunohistochemical profile are most consistent with 
metastatic adenocarcinoma of breast origin. 
Quantitative interpretation for ER, PR and Her-2neu will be performed 
separately and an addendum will follow.

submitted in cassette  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID .

sectioned. Submitted entirely in cassettes  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID . 
 
INTRA-OPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:

nuclei in the tumor cells is assessed visually and reported as follows:

incomplete membrane staining of tumor cells)

FINAL PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: 
A. LEFT OVARY AND FALLOPIAN TUBE, LEFT SALPINGO-OOPHORECTOMY: 
- High grade serous carcinoma involving the left ovary, fallopian tube and 
periadnexal soft tissue. (see note) 
 
B. UTERUS, RIGHT OVARY AND FALLOPIAN TUBE, HYSTERECTOMY AND RIGHT 
SALPINGO-OOPHORECTOMY: 
- High grade serous carcinoma involving the right ovary, fallopian tube, 
periadnexal soft tissue, and uterine serosa with invasion into the outer 
myometrium. (see note) 
- Metastatic poorly differentiated carcinoma with signet ring cell features, 
most consistent with breast origin, involving the lower uterine segment and 
cervix. Clinical correlation recommended. (see note) 
 
- Background atrophic endometrium with small endometrial polyp. 
- Background myometrium with leiomyomata and adenomyosis. 
- Serosal endometriosis. 
 
C. OMENTUM, EXCISION: 
- High grade serous carcinoma. (see note) 
 
Note: Both high grade serous carcinoma and a metastatic carcinoma with signet 
ring cell features (most consistent with breast carcinoma) are present in the 
uterus. Multiple microscopic foci of high grade serous carcinoma are present 
throughout the omentum, adnexa, and uterine serosa with invasion into the outer 
half of the myometrium. The overall distribution favors a peritoneal origin. 
Within the lower uterine segment endomyometrium and cervix is an infiltrative 
poorly differentiated carcinoma with signet ring cell features, which is 
morphologically distinct from the serous carcinoma. Immunohistochemical stains 
were performed on multiple blocks to differentiate between these various tumor 
foci. The tumor in the lower uterine segment/cervix (block  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) is positive for 
cytokeratin 7 and breast markers (GATA-3, mammoglobin, GCDFP-15) but negative 
for cytokeratin 20 and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID . The serous carcinoma in the omentum (block  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) 
demonstrates the opposite pattern ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  positive, negative for breast markers 
GATA-3, mammoglobin, GCDFP-15). Additionally, the tumor in the omentum is 
positive for  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  and completely negative for p53 (null p53). The tumor within 
the lower uterine segment and cervix is most consistent with metastatic breast 
carcinoma. An E-cadherin immunostain is negative, suggesting a lobular breast 
carcinoma. Clinical correlation is recommended. Immunohistochemical staining for 
estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /neu protein expression and 
fluorescence in-situ hybridization studies for  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /neu gene amplification have 
been ordered and will be reported in an addendum. Select slides shown in 
consultation to Dr. Robert Young, Esther Oliva, and Melinda Lerwill, who concur.

in the breast and that in cervix (positive in the former and negative in the 
latter). While the possibility of morphologic and immunohistochemical 
variability between primary and metastatic tumors cannot be excluded, clinical 
correlation is advised to exclude the possibility of a second, separate breast 
primary giving rise to the metastatic deposit in the uterine cervix.

TEST INFORMATION: 
In recent years, major efforts to define the molecular causes of cancer have 
revealed a wide number of genetic aberrations. A small subset of these defects, 
usually referred to as "drivers", is frequently present across cancer types and 
appears to be essential for oncogenesis and tumor progression. New drugs 
developed to selectively target such cancer-promoting pathways, are starting to 
complement the more conventional therapeutic approaches. While the clinical 
benefit observed with some targeted agents is encouraging, it has become clear 
that for such strategies to be successful, it will be necessary to identify the 
patient population carrying the genetic abnormalities targeted by each drug. 
 
We have developed a multiplexed allele-specific assay to detect somatic 
mutations in tumor DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples 
(Dias-Santagata  REMOVED_CASE_ID ). The SNaPshot Version 4 clinical test detects common 
mutations in 23 cancer genes. The SNaPshot multiplex assay tests for somatic 
variants at 90 different loci. Briefly, multiplex PCR using tumor DNA is 
followed by mutation detection using single base extension sequencing technology 
(SNaPshot, Applied Biosystems). In addition, a separate PCR reaction using 
primers flanking EGFR exon 19, EGFR exon 20 and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  exon 20 are used to detect 
in-frame activating insertions or deletions in EGFR and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  that may not be 
detected using SNaPshot. The mutations are visualized using an ABI  REMOVED_CASE_ID  DNA 
analyzer. The average analytic sensitivity of detecting mutations in this assay 
has been established in our laboratory at approximately 5% mutant allele.

No lymphovascular invasion is present. 
Mitoses in tumor cells number up to REMOVED_DATE HPF in the myoepithelial component and

NOTE: The tumor has an unusual biphasic morphology composed of clusters of 
epithelial cells distributed evenly throughout a background of spindle cells. 
The epithelial cells form tubular glands and nests which are PR positive and 
keratin positive ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID , Pan-K, Cam REMOVED_DATE and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /6). The spindle cells range 
from rounded to a more spindled appearance, have high grade nuclei, and these 
cells stain with keratin (Pan-K &  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /6) as well as the myoepithelial markers 
p63 and calponin consistent with myoepithelial differentiation. The tumor has a 
lobulated border which is irregular and infiltrative. 
The staining pattern excludes an unusual phyllodes tumor. A malignant 
adenomyoepithelioma is favored given the distinctive morphological appearance 
and supporting immunostains. Although criteria which predict local recurrence 
and the development of distant metastases are not definitively established, 
available reports in the literature suggest that the presence of myoepithelial 
and epithelial nuclear pleomorphism and atypia, along with mitoses > REMOVED_DATE HPF, 
necrosis, and a lobulated or infiltrative border favors a diagnosis of 
"malignant adenomyoepithelioma". The two largest series have been published by 
Drs. Tavassoli and Page (see references below). Dr. S. Lester, & Dr. A. 
Richardson have also reviewed this case and agree with the diagnosis.

One (1) sentinel lymph node negative for carcinoma (3 H&E levels examined).

One (1) sentinel lymph node negative for carcinoma (3 H&E levels examined). 
C. RIGHT BREAST NON SENTINEL NODE: 
One (1) lymph node negative for carcinoma.

No residual carcinoma present. 
Skin with scar and benign breast tissue with excision site changes. 
The margins were inked and evaluated for the final diagnosis. 
E. RIGHT BREAST MRI GUIDED, WIRE LOCALIZED EXCISION FOR AN AREA OF ENHANCEMENT: 
Fibroadenoma (0.9cm ) (see NOTE). 
Apocrine cysts and columnar cell hyperplasia (see NOTE). 
Excision site changes are also present. 
The margins were inked and evaluated for the final diagnosis. 
NOTE: The area of cysts and columnar cell hyperplasia forms a distinct focus 
measuring 1.7cm on the glass slide ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) and is located at the medial aspect of 
the specimen, likely correlating with an area of density at the medial end of 
the specimen in the accompanying radiograph. The fibroadenoma ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ,  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) is 
located in the middle of the specimen and abuts the anterior/inferior margin 
likely correlating with the circled area of interest in the accompanying 
radiograph. 
CLINICAL DATA: 
History: 46 yo F malignant adenomyoepithelioma s/p incisional biopsy with 
lateral margin < 0.1cm  Found to have small area of enhancement on MRI post 
to excisional biopsy. 
Operation: Right breast reexcision, sent lymph node biopsy. 
Operative Findings: Not provided. 
Clinical Diagnosis: Right breast cancer.

Micro  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID : 2 frags, ESS. 
Part C, "#4. Non-sent node right breast", consists of a tan-yellow irregular 
rubbery tissue, consistent with a lymph node (1.5 x REMOVED_DATE x 0.6cm ), which is 
inked blue, bisected and submitted in its entirety. 
Micro  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID : 2 frags, ESS. 
Part D, "#5. Lateral reexcision stitch on new margin", consists of an irregular 
portion of fibrofatty tissue (3.5 x REMOVED_DATE x 1.2cm ) with a suture along one 
aspect designating the new margin. This new margin is inked blue, and the 
opposite aspect is inked black. There is an overlying tan wrinkled skin 
ellipse, at the junction of the blue-inked and black-inked margin (3.7 x REMOVED_DATE 
cm). The specimen is serially sectioned to reveal 70% yellow lobulated adipose 
tissue, and 30% white fibrous tissue, with no discrete masses or lesions 
identified. The white fibrous tissue extends to the black and blue-inked 
margins. The specimen is sequentially submitted in its entirety. 
Micro  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID : Sequential cross sections,  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID , 2 frags each,  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID , 1

lateral", consists of an irregular portion of fibrofatty tissue (4.4 x REMOVED_DATE x 
1.8cm ), with a long suture designating lateral, and a short suture designating 
superior. The specimen is received previously inked per pathology protocol as 
superior red, inferior green, anterior blue, posterior black, medial orange and 
lateral yellow. There is an inserted needle-localization wire, as displayed on 
the accompanying radiograph, which enters along the lateral margin and exits 
along the medial margin. The radiograph demonstrated two densities - one 
abutting the medial margin and one abutting the inferior margin. The specimen 
is serially sectioned to reveal a dense white fibrous area, corresponding to 
the area of concern on the radiograph (2.0 x REMOVED_DATE x 1.0cm ). The dense white 
fibrous area is less than 0.1cm from the posterior margin, 0.5cm from the 
anterior margin, less than 0.1cm from the superior margin, less than 0.1cm 
from the inferior margin, 0.2cm from the lateral margin, and 1.0cm from the 
medial margin. The remaining cut surface displays 99% yellow lobulated adipose 
tissue, and 1% white fibrous tissue, with no additional discrete masses or 
lesions identified. The specimen is sequentially submitted in its entirety.

insertion/deletion (indel) detection in genomic DNA using next generation 
sequencing (NGS). Briefly, genomic DNA was isolated from a formalin-fixed

reactions. Illumina MiSeq 2 x 151 base paired-end sequencing results were

laboratory-developed insertion/deletion analysis algorithm were used for SNV and

Neutrophilic dermatitis with pan-dermal and subcutaneous involvement 
(see note) 
Fibroadipose tissue with acute inflammation and necrosis. 
Prior biopsy site.

A gram stain is negative for organisms; culture correlation 
is needed. 
B. LEFT BREAST, TISSUE, EXCISION: 
Neutrophilic dermatitis with pan-dermal and subcutaneous involvement 
(see note) 
COMMENT: 
Although it is difficult to exclude necrotizing fasciitis with certainty, the 
substantial pan-dermal infiltrate by neutrophils with associated superficial 
ulceration in the absence of primary endothelial occlusive alterations and 
zonal necrosis would favor pyoderma gangrenosum. The extent of subcutaneous 
involvement is, however, somewhat unusual for this entity, although secondary 
involvement from the overlying dermis and nature of sampling [debridement of 
more advanced regions] may in part account for this finding). It is 
recommended that the final diagnostic assessment also include consideration of 
correlative clinical parameters, notably exclusion of an infectious cause. In 
addition, if at anytime the clinical parameters continue to raise the 
possibility of necrotizing fasciitis (as opposed to an atypically deep/advanced 
manifestation of pyoderma gangrenosum), sampling of an early evolving lesion or 
lesion edge (as opposed to a debridement sampling) is suggested. 
Case referred by Surgical Pathology to Dermatopathology on REMOVED_DATE  and this 
diagnosis reflects this consultative review.

substantial pan-dermal infiltrate by neutrophils with associated superficial 
ulceration in the absence of primary endothelial occlusive alterations and 
zonal necrosis would favor pyoderma gangrenosum. The extent of subcutaneous 
involvement is, however, somewhat unusual for this entity, although secondary 
involvement from the overlying dermis and nature of sampling [debridement of 
more advanced regions] may in part account for this finding). It is 
recommended that the final diagnostic assessment also include consideration of 
correlative clinical parameters, notably exclusion of an infectious cause. In 
addition, if at anytime the clinical parameters continue to raise the 
possibility of necrotizing fasciitis (as opposed to an atypically deep/advanced 
manifestation of pyoderma gangrenosum), sampling of an early evolving lesion or 
lesion edge (as opposed to a debridement sampling) is suggested.

TEST INFORMATION: 
In recent years, major efforts to define the molecular causes of cancer have 
revealed a wide number of genetic aberrations. A small subset of these defects, 
usually referred to as"drivers", is frequently present across cancer types and 
appears to be essential for oncogenesis and tumor progression. New drugs 
developed to selectively target such cancer-promoting pathways, are starting to 
complement the more conventional therapeutic approaches. While the clinical 
benefit observed with some targeted agents is encouraging, it has become clear 
that for such strategies to be successful, it will be necessary to identify the 
patient population carrying the genetic abnormalities targeted by each drug. 
 
We have developed a multiplexed allele-specific assay to detect somatic 
mutations in tumor DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples 
(Dias-Santagata  REMOVED_CASE_ID ). The SNaPshot Version 4 clinical test detects common 
mutations in 23 cancer genes. The SNaPshot multiplex assay tests for somatic 
variants at 90 different loci. Briefly, multiplex PCR using tumor DNA is 
followed by mutation detection using single base extension sequencing technology 
(SNaPshot, Applied Biosystems). In addition, a separate PCR reaction using 
primers flanking EGFR exon 19, EGFR exon 20 and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  exon 20 are used to detect 
in-frame activating insertions or deletions in EGFR and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  that may not be 
detected using SNaPshot. The mutations are visualized using an ABI  REMOVED_CASE_ID  DNA 
analyzer. The average analytic sensitivity of detecting mutations in this assay 
has been established in our laboratory at approximately 5% mutant allele.

patient. The preliminary results were communicated to Dr. Hughes in person at

- Flat epithelial atypia. 
- Fibrocystic changes. 
- Small radial scar.

carcinoma cells show membranous positivity for E-cadherin. The in-situ carcinoma 
cells are largely positive for E-cadherin, although scattered small foci are 
negative. Classification of the invasive and in-situ carcinomas as having ductal 
and lobular features is based on combined morphologic and immunohistochemical 
assessment. Immunohistochemical stains for E-cadherin were examined on 5 blocks.

TEST INFORMATION: 
In recent years, major efforts to define the molecular causes of cancer have 
revealed a wide number of genetic aberrations. A small subset of these defects, 
usually referred to as "drivers", is frequently present across cancer types and 
appears to be essential for oncogenesis and tumor progression. New drugs 
developed to selectively target such cancer-promoting pathways, are starting to 
complement the more conventional therapeutic approaches. While the clinical 
benefit observed with some targeted agents is encouraging, it has become clear 
that for such strategies to be successful, it will be necessary to identify the 
patient population carrying the genetic abnormalities targeted by each drug. 
 
We have developed a multiplexed allele-specific assay to detect somatic 
mutations in tumor DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples 
(Dias-Santagata  REMOVED_CASE_ID ). The assay SNaPshot Version 3 detects mutations in 68 
different loci from 14 cancer genes. Briefly, multiplex PCR using tumor DNA is 
followed by mutation detection using single base extension sequencing technology 
(SNaPshot, Applied Biosystems). In addition, a separate PCR reaction using 
primers flanking EGFR exon 19, EGFR exon 20 and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  exon 20 are used to detect 
in-frame activating insertions or deletions in EGFR and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  that may not be 
detected using SNaPshot. The mutations are visualized using an ABI  REMOVED_CASE_ID  DNA 
analyzer. The average analytic sensitivity of detecting mutations in this assay 
has been established in our laboratory at approximately 5% mutant allele.

usually referred to as "drivers", is frequently present across cancer types and

developed to selectively target such cancer-promoting pathways, are starting to 
complement the more conventional therapeutic approaches. While the clinical 
benefit observed with some targeted agents is encouraging, it has become clear 
that for such strategies to be successful, it will be necessary to identify the 
patient population carrying the genetic abnormalities targeted by each drug.

analyzer. The average analytic sensitivity of detecting mutations in this assay 
has been established in our laboratory at approximately 5% mutant allele.

TEST INFORMATION: 
Aberrations involving the fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) gene have 
been noted in tumors of multiple types, including certain lung, breast, ovarian, 
skeletal muscle, melanocytic and hematopoietic neoplasms. [1] Amplification of 
the  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  gene was recently identified as a significant and common finding (22% 
by FISH) in a cohort of squamous cell carcinomas of the lung. [2] 
 
The assay performed on this patient uses fluorescence in situ hybridization 
(FISH) on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor specimens to analyze  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  gene 
amplification status. Briefly, 5-micron sections of formalin-fixed 
paraffin-embedded tumor material were prepared and an H&E section reviewed to 
select regions for hybridization that contain a majority of tumor cells. A 
dual-color FISH assay was performed using Bacterial Artificial Chromosome probe 
CTD- REMOVED_CASE_ID  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  (chromosome 8p,  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  locus, home-brew) and a copy number probe 
(centromere 8; Abbott-Vysis 06 REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  or 06 REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ). 
 
Signal quantitation was used to generate a  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /centromere 8 ratio.  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  to 
Centromere 8 ratios are interpreted as follows: REMOVED_DATE to REMOVED_DATE is considered 
borderline for amplification; REMOVED_DATE to REMOVED_DATE is considered low-level amplification; 
and greater than REMOVED_DATE or clustered  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  signals that are too numerous to count 
would be considered highly amplified. CPT codes for this assay are  REMOVED_CASE_ID  x 2.

sequencing (NGS). Briefly, genomic DNA was isolated from a formalin-fixed

RIGHT BREAST SIMPLE MASTECTOMY: 
SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA OF LACTIFEROUS DUCTS with associated subareolar chronic 
granulomatous inflammation, see NOTE 
Uninvolved breast parenchyma with apocrine cysts. 
Skin with scar and prior procedure site changes. 
NOTE: Squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts (SMOLD) is also known as 
recurrent subareolar abscess and periductal mastitis. This unusual disease is 
mostly seen in smokers where it presents as a painful erythematous subareolar 
mass which fails to heal following incision and drainage of the "abscess". The 
pathology is keratinizing squamous metaplasia deep in the nipple ducts which 
causes them to dilate and then rupture producing a non-infectious chronic 
granulomatous inflammatory response (the "abscess") which often drains to the 
overlying skin as a purulent exudate via the offending nipple duct or a sinus 
tract.

anterior to posterior. The specimen is covered by a skin ellipse, measuring 
13.5cm x 7.0cm with 3.0cm areola, centered by a 1.4cm everted nipple (0.7 
cm anterior to posterior). There is a 2.5cm well-healed scar in the lateral
